newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND SET PAKISTAN 276 TO WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND SET PAKISTAN 276 TO WIN.

text.p: Pakistan were set a difficult victory target of 276 after New Zealand were bowled out for 311 in their second innings at tea on the third day of the first test on Saturday.
New Zealand, 178 for five at lunch, were eventually dismissed for 311, with their last-wtnership delaying the tea inverval.
Stephen Fleming and Chris Cairns shared a sixth-wicket stand of 141 to put their side on top but both narrowly missed their centuries.
Cairns batted freely to make 93 from 89 balls while the left-handed Fleming was stranded on 92 after the last man Simon Doull was stumpe
Cairns slammed 13 fours and three sixes, all of them from off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq. Fleming had 13 fours and a six in his highest test score.
New Zealand had a minor middle-order collapse following the departure of Cairns when Chris Harris, Lee Germon and Dipak Patel fell in quick succession.
But Fleming and Doull added an important 48 runs for the last wicket to push the total beyond 300.
Mushtaq Ahmad was the best bowler with six for 86 for a match bag of 10 for 171, the second 10-wicket haul of his career.
